{{Short description|Mathematical concept}}
In [[functional analysis]], a '''uniform algebra''' ''A'' on a [[compact space|compact]] [[Hausdorff space|Hausdorff]] [[topological space|space]] ''X'' is a [[closed set|closed]] (with respect to the [[uniform norm]]) [[algebra over a field|subalgebra]] of the [[C*-algebra]] ''C''(''X'') (the [[continuous function|continuous]] [[complex number|complex]]-valued functions on ''X'') with the following properties:<ref>{{harv|Gamelin|2005|p=25}}</ref>
: the constant functions are contained in ''A''
: for every <math>x, y \in X</math> there is <math>f \in A</math> with <math>f(x) \ne f(y)</math>. This is called separating the points of ''X''.

As a closed subalgebra of the [[commutative algebra (structure)]] [[Banach algebra]] ''C''(''X''), a uniform algebra is itself a unital commutative Banach algebra (when equipped with the uniform norm). Hence, it is (by definition) a [[Banach function algebra]].

A uniform algebra ''A'' on ''X'' is said to be '''natural''' if the [[maximal ideal]]s of ''A'' are precisely the [[ideal (ring theory)|ideal]]s <math>M_x</math> of functions vanishing at a point ''x'' in ''X''.

== Abstract characterization ==
If ''A'' is a [[unital algebra|unital]] commutative Banach algebra such that <math>\|a^2\| = \|a\|^2</math> for all ''a'' in ''A'', then there is a compact Hausdorff ''X'' such that ''A'' is [[isomorphic]] as a Banach algebra to a uniform algebra on ''X''. This result follows from the [[spectral radius formula]] and the [[Gelfand representation]].
